advances: An exact fixed-family statement for positive buffers, arbitrary norms and positive concave base multipliers. It retains the closed weighted pure-base branch.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The energy-power profile $E_{C_z}(y)^{1/(d+1)}$ is continuous and zero on own boundaries by the proof of 0b2fbdaf8d3134a0, which uses the actual finite positive compatible family. A complete affine lattice can be identified with an ordinary integer lattice in affine base coordinates, without changing the fiber measure or the set of tested affine margins. In rank zero one can place the single base at zero in one ambient base coordinate. In particular $E^{1/d}$ is continuous as a power of this profile. It is jointly concave on the own-interior domain by 5aeb5916857f97a9 and remains concave on the hull by continuity and approximation within each fiber. The increasing concave weighted geometric mean of $E^{1/d}$ and $\ell$, with weights $d/(d+1)$ and $1/(d+1)$, proves joint concavity of $f$.

For a fixed nonvertical observable $N(z,X)=a\cdot z+u\cdot X$ its upper tail is continuous, since every level has zero $d$-volume in each fiber. For $0<q\le M$, the thresholds of mass at least $q$ form a closed interval unbounded on the left, with right endpoint $c_q(N)$. Thus each nonvertical superlevel condition is the closed convex inequality $Nw-\varepsilon f(w)\Gamma(u)\le c_q(N)$. The pure-base superlevel is convex by the usual halfspace argument: a halfspace containing a convex combination contains some input. It is closed, since for every fixed base direction the condition is a closed linear upper bound at its right quantile, using the left-continuous closed atomic tail. The intersection over all directions gives the compact convex superlevel in $C$. This yields attainment on the finite union of compact sampled fibers, and combining deepest marks at any integer anchored base proves completeness of $I$.

At an own boundary $f=0$, and the nonvertical zero-mass supporting cap in the proof of 55a57b1cf55d0c87 gives zero buffered depth. For Euclidean unit $u$, use 1ec728c26c11b368 at threshold $u\cdot y-\varepsilon f(p,y)\Gamma(u)$: the minimum over base tilts is attained and continuous in $(u,t)$. The composite threshold is continuous on the unit sphere for any norm $\Gamma$, so minimizing over that sphere attains the nonvertical branch. This supplies an attaining cap at every mark with a strict base gap. If its own trace were full, the norm-independent whole-fiber capture part of 3dd858960f824a5d would give mass at least $b_{\rm base}(p)$. The buffered trace includes a neighborhood of the mark, so the minimizing trace is proper. At $p\in A$, any own buffered trace missing a point misses a set of positive volume because its exclusion is strict and $K_p$ is a convex body. Choose a pure-base mass-$Q$ cap through $p$, attained since the base has finitely many traces, and add a sufficiently large finite multiple of its base normal to the omitted direction. Strictly included base fibers are then full and strictly excluded ones empty. Boundary fibers contribute at most their original full masses, and the own fiber strictly less. This contradicts buffered depth $Q$ and proves the full-trace assertion.

The combined mark $w_r$ is deepest by convexity. Take any attaining nonvertical cap there, scale to $\Gamma(u)=1$, and put $c=Nw_r-\varepsilon f(w_r)$. Its proper own cut makes the continuous mass-$Q$ tail strictly decreasing near $c$, because every nearby nontrivial threshold increment removes a positive own-fiber slab. Thus $c=c_Q(N)$. At every input, $Nw_j-\varepsilon f(w_j)\le c$. Their weighted sum and $Nw_r=c+\varepsilon f(w_r)$ give $f(w_r)\le\sum_j\lambda_j f(w_j)$. Concavity gives the reverse inequality, so equality holds and every input threshold equals $c$. This proves that the same cap is active at each mark.

Set $F_j=E_{K_{p_j}}(y_j)^{1/d}$ and $F_r=E_{K_r}(y_r)^{1/d}$. All $F_j,F_r$ and multiplier values are positive. Because the weighted geometric mean is strictly increasing in both positive coordinates, its equality chain forces $F_r=\sum_j\lambda_jF_j$ and $\ell(r)=\sum_j\lambda_j\ell(p_j)$. Equality in the mean also forces the ratios $F_j/\ell(p_j)$ to be constant. Indeed writing the mean as $\ell(F/\ell)^{d/(d+1)}$, its concavity inequality is Jensen's inequality for the strictly concave power with normalized weights proportional to $\lambda_j\ell(p_j)$. The ratio at $r$ is the same. By 5aeb5916857f97a9 with the actual $K_r$ as containing body, the whole $K_{p_j}-y_j$ are positive homothets and $K_r$ equals their Minkowski combination before recentering. By affine covariance of energy from d90ba05577427854 their homothety ratios are the ratios of the $F_j$. These equal the ratios of the multipliers, giving the common body $K_*$ and the asserted scale at $r$. The geometric mean formula then gives the common positive $c_*=f(w_j)/\ell(p_j)=f(w_r)/\ell(r)$. At each of those marks the same cap in the normalized fiber is $\{X\in K_*:u\cdot X\ge-\varepsilon c_*\}$. It is proper at $r$, so it is proper at every input. Full traces at atomic marks exclude every input in $A$.

statement:
Let $P$ be a finite nonempty complete base in an affine lattice, and let $K_p\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, be positive compact convex fibers with the anchored Minkowski inclusions $\sum_j\lambda_j K_{p_j}\subseteq K_p$ whenever $\sum_j\lambda_jp_j=p\in P$ for convex weights. Let $C$ be the hull of their lifts, with real fibers $C_z$, and let $\mu$ be the sum of their $d$-volumes, with total $M$. Take $\ell>0$ continuous and concave on $\operatorname{conv}P$, $\varepsilon>0$, and a norm $\Gamma$ on continuous covectors. Put $f(z,y)=(\ell(z)E_{C_z}(y)/M)^{1/(d+1)}$, where $E_K(y)$ is the marked projective energy $\inf_b\int_K(1+b\cdot(X-y))^{-d-1}\,dX$ over denominators positive throughout $K$, extended by zero on own-fiber boundaries.

At a real mark $w=(p,y)\in C$, define its raw buffered depth as the minimum of its closed pure-base depth $b_{\rm base}(p)$ for weights $|K_z|$ and the infimum of the masses of all caps
$$
a\cdot(z-p)+u\cdot(X-y)\ge-\varepsilon f(w)\Gamma(u),\qquad u\ne0.
$$
The whole-base trace is allowed. Write $Q$ for the supremum at sampled marks and assume $0<Q<M$. Let $I$ be its deepest bases, and set $J=\{p\in I:b_{\rm base}(p)>Q\}$ and $A=I\setminus J$. The maximum is attained and its real superlevel is convex, so $I=P\cap\operatorname{conv}I$. Every deepest mark is own-interior. At every deepest mark in $A$ all own buffered traces are full. At every deepest mark in $J$ a nonvertical attaining cap exists and every such cap has a proper own trace.

Suppose $r=\sum_j\lambda_jp_j\in J$, with $\lambda_j>0$, $\sum_j\lambda_j=1$, $p_j\in I$. Choose any deepest marks $w_j=(p_j,y_j)$, and set $w_r=\sum_j\lambda_j w_j=(r,y_r)$. Every $p_j$ lies in $J$. More precisely, any active nonvertical cap at $w_r$ is the same active cap at each $w_j$. For one convex body $K_*$ containing zero in its interior, the whole fibers satisfy $K_{p_j}=y_j+\ell(p_j)K_*$ and $K_r=y_r+\ell(r)K_*$. Also $\ell(r)=\sum_j\lambda_j\ell(p_j)$ and $f(w_j)/\ell(p_j)=f(w_r)/\ell(r)>0$. After these rescalings the cap has the identical proper trace at every input and the target.
title: A proper buffered deepest source inherits only proper deepest inputs
